ことになっても構わないと？
records.previous_English: Even if we end up controlling the Caribbean?
records.english: Even if we end up controlling the Caribbean?
records.localization_note: The question tests the boundaries of the offer.

records.speaker: Diogo Escante
records.context: The guildmaster introduces Escante, who asks Hodram to act against Maldonado on Spain's behalf. Hodram tests the political bargain and can solicit Gerhard's private advice before he accepts.
records.source_meaning: Escante prefers a friendly power to someone who attacks transport ships indiscriminately.
records.Japanese:
輸送船に無差別攻撃を仕掛けるような
男がのさばっているよりは
我々に友好的な勢力がとりしきって
いてくれたほうが、百倍望ましい
records.previous_English: I'd much rather have a friendly power in charge than a man who attacks transport ships indiscriminately.
records.english: I'd much rather have a friendly power in charge than a man who attacks transport ships indiscriminately.
records.localization_note: The comparison protects his stated trade concerns.

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.context: The guildmaster introduces Escante, who asks Hodram to act against Maldonado on Spain's behalf. Hodram tests the political bargain and can solicit Gerhard's private advice before he accepts.
records.source_meaning: Hodram suspects that Escante finds them easier to deal with than the English.
records.Japanese:
ふっ。イギリスが来るのは困るが
俺たちであればくみしやすいという
ことか
records.previous_English: Heh. You don't want the English here, but you think we'll be easier to handle.
records.english: Heh. You don't want the English here, but you think we'll be easier to handle.
records.localization_note: The dry laugh makes his skepticism clear.

records.speaker: Diogo Escante
records.context: The guildmaster introduces Escante, who asks Hodram to act against Maldonado on Spain's behalf. Hodram tests the political bargain and can solicit Gerhard's private advice before he accepts.
records.source_meaning: Escante asks Hodram not to read it that way.
records.Japanese:
…そう、勘ぐらんでもらいたい
ものだな
records.previous_English: I'd prefer you didn't read it that way.
records.english: I'd prefer you didn't read it that way.
records.localization_note: The cool restraint is part of the negotiation.

records.speaker: Diogo Escante
records.context: The guildmaster introduces Escante, who asks Hodram to act against Maldonado on Spain's behalf. Hodram tests the political bargain and can solicit Gerhard's private advice before he accepts.
records.source_meaning: Spain and England are at war, so Escante cannot openly join England.
records.Japanese:
イギリスと本国とは全面的な交戦状態に
ある。おおっぴらにイギリスと
組むことはできん
records.previous_English: Spain is at war with England. We cannot openly join the English.
records.english: Spain is at war with England. We cannot openly join the English.
records.localization_note: The diplomatic constraint answers Hodram's suspicion.

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.context: The guildmaster introduces Escante, who asks Hodram to act against Maldonado on Spain's behalf. Hodram tests the political bargain and can solicit Gerhard's private advice before he accepts.
records.source_meaning: Hodram points out that they are also Protestants, whom Spain's king hates.
records.Japanese:
俺たちも、スペイン王が殺したいほど
憎んでいる新教徒だが？
records.previous_English: We're Protestants too. Wouldn't your king gladly see us dead?
records.english: We're Protestants too. Wouldn't your king gladly see us dead?
records.localization_note: The pointed question challenges the distinction Escante is drawing.

records.speaker: Diogo Escante
records.context: The guildmaster introduces Escante, who asks Hodram to act against Maldonado on Spain's behalf. Hodram tests the political bargain and can solicit Gerhard's private advice before he accepts.
records.source_meaning: Escante wants the religious wars kept in Europe but makes an exception for England.
records.Japanese:
宗教戦争は、ヨーロッパでやって
くれればいい。私としては新大陸にまで
そんな無意味な対立を持ち込む気は
毛頭ない。しかし、イギリスは違う！
records.previous_English: Let Europe keep its religious wars. I won't drag that senseless conflict to the New World. England is different!
records.english: Let Europe keep its religious wars. I won't drag that senseless conflict to the New World. England is different!
records.localization_note: The abrupt exception signals a shift from policy to personal hostility.

records.speaker: Diogo Escante
records.context: The guildmaster introduces Escante, who asks Hodram to act against Maldonado on Spain's behalf. Hodram tests the political bargain and can solicit Gerhard's private advice before he accepts.
records.source_meaning: Escante calls England Spain's sworn enemy and recoils at its flag in these waters.
records.Japanese:
ヤツらは特別…、スペイン国民の
不倶戴天の敵だ！　この海域にイギリス
王国の国旗がたなびく光景など、想像
するだけでもおぞましいことだよ！
records.previous_English: The English are Spain's sworn enemies! The very thought of their flag flying over these waters disgusts me!
records.english: The English are Spain's sworn enemies! The very thought of their flag flying over these waters disgusts me!
records.localization_note: The visual image and disgust preserve his forceful prejudice.

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.context: The guildmaster introduces Escante, who asks Hodram to act against Maldonado on Spain's behalf. Hodram tests the political bargain and can solicit Gerhard's private advice before he accepts.
records.source_meaning: Hodram stays silent.
records.localization_note: The silence lets Escante continue the pitch.

records.speaker: Diogo Escante
records.context: The guildmaster introduces Escante, who asks Hodram to act against Maldonado on Spain's behalf. Hodram tests the political bargain and can solicit Gerhard's private advice before he accepts.
records.source_meaning: Escante says the alliance benefits Hodram because Caribbean expansion would bring him up against Maldonado anyway.
records.Japanese:
君たちにとっても損な話ではないと
思うが…。カリブ海進出を狙うので
あれば、マルドナードを相手にしない
わけにもいくまい
records.previous_English: This benefits you as well. If you mean to expand into the Caribbean, you'll have to face Maldonado sooner or later.
records.english: This benefits you as well. If you mean to expand into the Caribbean, you'll have to face Maldonado sooner or later.
records.localization_note: The argument gives Hodram a strategic incentive without assuming he has already decided.

records.speaker: Diogo Escante
records.context: The guildmaster introduces Escante, who asks Hodram to act against Maldonado on Spain's behalf. Hodram tests the political bargain and can solicit Gerhard's private advice before he accepts.
records.source_meaning: Maldonado rose through piracy, remains a formidable admiral with a powerful fleet, and would be hard to face alone.
records.Japanese:
彼も、海賊あがりの豪腕提督だ
今でも現役で、強力な船団を率いて
いる。君たちの力だけでは
もてあますだろう
records.previous_English: He came up through piracy and he's a formidable admiral. He still commands a powerful fleet. You'd have a hard time facing him alone.
records.english: He rose through piracy. He's a formidable admiral. His fleet is still strong. You'd struggle against him alone.
records.localization_note: Keeps Escante's assessment and why he thinks Hodram needs help.

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.context: The guildmaster introduces Escante, who asks Hodram to act against Maldonado on Spain's behalf. Hodram tests the political bargain and can solicit Gerhard's private advice before he accepts.
records.source_meaning: Hodram sees the logic and the chance to build strength.
records.Japanese:
…理屈は分かった
こちらとしても、力を蓄える好機…
records.previous_English: ...I see your reasoning. It would give us a chance to build our strength...
records.english: ...I see your reasoning. It would give us a chance to build our strength...
records.localization_note: The hesitation signals consideration even in the assent path.

records.speaker: Gerhard Adernkatz
records.context: The guildmaster introduces Escante, who asks Hodram to act against Maldonado on Spain's behalf. Hodram tests the political bargain and can solicit Gerhard's private advice before he accepts.
records.source_meaning: Gerhard privately sees the split as a chance to gain strength and advises against making enemies of both sides.
records.Japanese:
（…こちらとしても、スペイン領の
　分裂につけこんで、力を蓄える
　好機です。両者を敵にまわすのは
　得策ではありません。）
records.previous_English: (This split in Spain's colonies is our chance to gain strength. Making both sides enemies would be unwise.)
records.english: (This split in Spain's colonies is our chance to gain strength. Making both sides enemies would be unwise.)
records.localization_note: The aside preserves the strategic calculation and his role as adviser.

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.context: The guildmaster introduces Escante, who asks Hodram to act against Maldonado on Spain's behalf. Hodram tests the political bargain and can solicit Gerhard's private advice before he accepts.
records.source_meaning: Hodram considers Gerhard's advice.
records.Japanese: ふむ…
records.previous_English: Hm...
records.english: Hm...
records.localization_note: The short acknowledgment leaves the decision to Hodram.

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.context: The guildmaster introduces Escante, who asks Hodram to act against Maldonado on Spain's behalf. Hodram tests the political bargain and can solicit Gerhard's private advice before he accepts.
records.source_meaning: Hodram agrees to accept the proposal.
records.Japanese:
いいだろう
その話、乗ってみることにする
records.previous_English: Very well. We'll accept.
records.english: Very well. We'll accept.
records.localization_note: The concise assent settles the negotiation after either response.

records.speaker: Diogo Escante
records.context: The guildmaster introduces Escante, who asks Hodram to act against Maldonado on Spain's behalf. Hodram tests the political bargain and can solicit Gerhard's private advice before he accepts.
records.source_meaning: Escante is relieved Hodram sees reason.
records.Japanese:
君が、物分かりの悪い人物でなくて
安心したよ
records.previous_English: I'm glad you see reason.
records.english: I'm glad you see reason.
records.localization_note: The polite wording leaves a trace of Escante's condescension.
